CEO COMMENTARY
Harris H. Simmons, Chairman and CEO of Zions Bancorporation, commented, “Third quarter earnings per share increased 20% to $1.78, up from $1.48 a year ago. The higher earnings were primarily a reflection of improved credit quality, as net loan charge-offs were $3 million, down from $56 million a year ago. Although an increased pace of loan payoffs, combined with a highly competitive market, produced flat loan growth compared to the second quarter, customer deposits grew nearly 10% annualized from second quarter levels.”
Mr. Simmons continued, “Short- and medium-term interest rates began to rise in the last month of the quarter, and we expect that our moderately asset-sensitive balance sheet should produce stronger net interest income in a higher rate environment, while we're seeing continued improvement in noninterest income that we expect will continue into next year.”
Mr. Simmons concluded, “We were pleased to complete the acquisition of Basis Multifamily Finance I, LLC, a subsidiary of Basis Investment Group, at the end of July. This multifamily finance platform becomes an important strategic advantage in serving our commercial real estate clients, particularly in the fast-growing western markets we serve.”

Net interest income increased $12 million, or 2%, in the third quarter of 2026, compared with the prior year period. The increase was primarily driven by lower funding costs and changes in the balance sheet mix, including growth in average loans and leases, money market investments, and deposits, partially offset by a decline in investment securities. Deposit growth outpaced loan growth, reducing reliance on higher-cost borrowed funds and contributing to higher money market investment balances. While these factors contributed to higher net interest income, the net interest margin declined to 3.23% from 3.28% in the prior year period.
The yield on average interest-earning assets, net of hedging activity, was 4.91% for the third quarter of 2026, compared with 5.16% in the prior year period, primarily reflecting lower interest rates. The net yield on average loans and leases declined 28 basis points to 5.63%, while the net yield on average investment securities decreased 9 basis points to 2.64%. The yield on average money market investments decreased 76 basis points to 3.91%, as these short-term assets repriced more quickly in the declining rate environment.
The rate paid on total deposits and interest-bearing liabilities decreased to 1.75% for the third quarter of 2026 from 1.92% in the prior year period, reflecting lower interest rates and reduced short-term borrowings. The total cost of deposits declined to 1.59% from 1.67%, as the benefit of lower interest rates was partially offset by growth in higher-cost interest-bearing deposits, which reduced reliance on more costly short-term borrowings. Compared with the prior quarter, total cost of deposits increased from 1.48%, driven in part by a shift in deposit mix toward higher-cost interest-bearing deposits and an accounting presentation change that increased the total cost of deposits by approximately three basis points.
Average interest-earning assets increased $2.6 billion, or 3%, compared with the prior year period, reflecting growth in average money market investments of $1.8 billion and average loans and leases of $1.7 billion, partially offset by a $786 million decline in average investment securities. The increase in money market investments primarily reflected excess liquidity from deposit growth that exceeded loan growth, after first reducing short-term borrowings.

Average interest-bearing liabilities decreased $141 million, or less than 1%, compared with the prior year period. The decline was primarily driven by a $2.6 billion reduction in average borrowed funds, largely reflecting lower levels of short-term borrowings. This decrease was partially offset by a $2.4 billion increase in average interest-bearing deposits and higher average long-term debt balances resulting from senior note issuances completed over the past year. Average noninterest-bearing deposits increased $1.2 billion, or 5%, compared with the prior year period.

Customer-related noninterest income increased $29 million, or 18%, compared with the prior year period, reflecting broad-based growth across nearly all revenue streams. Capital markets fees and income increased $22 million, largely reflecting changes in net CVA. Excluding the impact of net CVA changes, capital markets fees and income increased $1 million due to higher swap fee revenue. Wealth management fees increased $2 million, reflecting growth in portfolio management and personal trust fees. Retail and business banking fees also increased $2 million, primarily due to higher overdraft service fees.
Noncustomer-related noninterest income decreased $21 million, or 81%, compared with the prior year period, primarily due to a $15 million decline in net securities gains, reflecting lower valuation adjustments in our Small Business Investment Company (“SBIC”) investment portfolio relative to the prior year quarter. Sequentially, net securities gains decreased $273 million, primarily due to notable pre-tax gains recognized in the preceding quarter from the sale of Class B-1 shares of Visa, Inc. and unrealized gains within the SBIC portfolio. Dividends and other income decreased $6 million, primarily due to a gain on the sale of bank-owned property and higher FHLB stock dividends in the prior year period.

Noninterest expense increased $26 million, or 5%, compared with the prior year quarter. Salaries and employee benefits expense increased $8 million, primarily due to higher incentive compensation accruals driven by year-over-year improvement in performance metrics, as well as increased employee benefits costs. Professional and legal services expense increased $6 million, primarily reflecting higher costs for outsourced services. Technology, telecom, and information processing expense increased $6 million, driven by higher application software, licensing, and maintenance costs.
Marketing and business development expense increased $3 million, largely due to customer acquisition and deposit growth initiatives. Other noninterest expense increased $3 million, reflecting higher miscellaneous operating costs, partially offset by a lower success fee accrual associated with SBIC investments. These increases were partially offset by a $4 million decrease in deposit insurance and regulatory expense, primarily attributable to higher FDIC assessment costs in the prior year quarter associated with the level of classified loans.
Adjusted noninterest expense increased $29 million, or 6%, consistent with the factors discussed above. The efficiency ratio was 61.9%, compared with 59.6%, and improved from 62.2% in the preceding quarter. For more information regarding non-GAAP financial measures, see pages 19-22.

Loans and leases, net of unearned income and fees, increased $2.2 billion, or 4%, to $62.5 billion, compared with the prior year quarter. This growth was primarily driven by a $1.3 billion increase in commercial loans, largely within the commercial and industrial loan portfolio, along with a $678 million increase in commercial real estate loans, mainly within the term loan portfolio.
The $166 million decrease in loans held for sale compared to the prior year quarter primarily reflects higher loan sale activity, including both recurring flow sales and portfolio sales, resulting in lower balances of real estate capital markets loans and 1-4 family residential loans held at period end.

During the third quarter of 2026, the provision for credit losses was an $8 million benefit, compared with a $49 million provision expense in the prior year quarter. The allowance for credit losses (“ACL”) totaled $696 million at September 30, 2026, compared with $725 million at September 30, 2025. The year-over-year decline in the ACL primarily reflects changes in loan portfolio composition and lower reserves associated with commercial real estate (“CRE”) portfolio-specific risks, partially offset by less favorable economic forecasts, adjustments to economic scenario weightings, and increased lending activity. The ratio of ACL to total loans and leases was 1.11% at September 30, 2026, compared with 1.20% at September 30, 2025.

Net loan and lease charge-offs totaled $3 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with $56 million in the prior year quarter. The prior year quarter included $50 million of charge-offs on revolving credit facilities to two related commercial borrowers that financed commercial mortgage originations and purchases.
At September 30, 2026, nonperforming assets totaled $315 million, or 0.50% of total loans and leases and other real estate owned, compared with $324 million, or 0.54%, in the prior year period. Nonperforming assets were primarily concentrated within the commercial and industrial, consumer 1-4 family residential, commercial owner-occupied, and commercial real estate term loan portfolios. Classified loans declined to $2.1 billion, or 3.40% of total loans and leases, compared with $2.4 billion, or 4.00%, in the prior year period, driven mainly by reductions in classified CRE exposures, largely attributable to loan payoffs.

Total deposits increased $3.1 billion, or 4%, compared with the prior year quarter, primarily driven by a $2.8 billion increase in interest-bearing deposits, largely reflecting the impact of deposit growth initiatives.
Customer deposits, excluding brokered deposits, increased $3.4 billion, or 5%, to $74.5 billion from $71.1 billion. These balances included approximately $6.6 billion and $6.8 billion of reciprocal deposits, respectively. The loan-to-deposit ratio was 80%, compared with 81% in the prior year quarter, reflecting deposit growth that outpaced loan growth.
Total borrowed funds decreased $1.8 billion, or 35%, compared with the prior year quarter, primarily reflecting a $2.7 billion reduction in short-term borrowings, driven by a decrease in short-term FHLB advances. This decline was partially offset by increases in federal funds purchased, security repurchase agreements, and $1.0 billion of senior notes issued over the past year.

The common stock dividend was $0.48 per share, compared with $0.45 per share during the third quarter of 2025. Common shares outstanding decreased 2.7 million from the third quarter of 2025, primarily due to common stock repurchases. During the third quarter of 2026, we repurchased 1.1 million common shares outstanding for $75 million. We did not repurchase any common shares during the prior year period.
At September 30, 2026, the accumulated other comprehensive income (loss) (“AOCI”) balance reflected a net loss of $2.0 billion, primarily attributable to declines in the fair value of fixed-rate AFS securities resulting from changes in interest rates. Included in this balance were $1.4 billion of unrealized losses ($1.1 billion after tax) associated with securities previously transferred from AFS to held-to-maturity (“HTM”).
Compared with September 30, 2025, AOCI improved by $67 million, primarily driven by the amortization of unrealized losses associated with the securities transferred from AFS to HTM and paydowns on AFS securities, partially offset by declines in the fair value of AFS securities. Compared with June 30, 2026, AOCI decreased by $122 million, primarily reflecting declines in the fair value of AFS securities resulting from increases in market interest rates during the quarter. We use pay-fixed, receive-floating interest rate swaps designated as hedges of our AFS securities to reduce the volatility of our AOCI balance.
Estimated common equity tier 1 (“CET1”) capital was $8.3 billion, an increase of 7% from $7.7 billion in the prior year period. The estimated CET1 capital ratio increased to 11.8% from 11.3%. Tangible book value per common share increased 13% to $43.50, primarily reflecting growth in retained earnings and lower unrealized losses recorded in AOCI. The increase was partially offset by $229 million of additional goodwill and intangible assets resulting from the July 2026 acquisition of the Basis Multifamily Finance agency lending platform. For more information on non-GAAP financial measures, see pages 19-22.

About Zions Bancorporation, N.A.
Zions Bancorporation, N.A. is one of the nation's premier financial services companies with annual net revenue of $3.4 billion in 2025, and total assets of approximately $89 billion at December 31, 2025. The Bank operates principally through seven separately managed, geographically defined bank divisions, each operating under its own local brand and management, and serving customers primarily in 11 Western states: Arizona, California, Colorado, Idaho, Nevada, New Mexico, Oregon, Texas, Utah, Washington, and Wyoming.
Zions is a consistent recipient of national and state-level customer survey awards recognizing excellence in small- and middle-market banking. It is also a leader in public finance advisory services and Small Business Administration lending. Zions is included in both the S&P MidCap 400 and NASDAQ Financial 100 indices. Additional investor information, along with links to local banking brands, is available at www.zionsbancorporation.com.

NON-GAAP FINANCIAL MEASURES
(Unaudited)
This press release includes certain non-GAAP financial measures alongside those prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”). Reconciliations between the applicable GAAP measures and the corresponding non-GAAP measures are provided in the accompanying schedules. We believe these adjustments are relevant to evaluating ongoing operating results and offer a meaningful basis for comparing performance across periods. Management uses these non-GAAP measures to assess both financial performance and position. Presenting these measures enables investors to evaluate our results using the same approach applied by management and commonly used within the financial services industry.
Non-GAAP financial measures have inherent limitations and may not be directly comparable to similar measures reported by other financial institutions. While these measures are commonly used by stakeholders to evaluate company performance, they should be viewed as supplemental and not as a substitute for analysis of results prepared in accordance with GAAP. Non-GAAP measures should not be considered in isolation, as they provide an incomplete perspective without reference to GAAP-based financial information.
Tangible Common Equity and Related Measures
Tangible common equity and related metrics are non-GAAP measures that exclude the impact of intangible assets and associated amortization. Management believes these measures provide meaningful insight into the utilization of shareholders’ equity and offer a consistent basis for evaluating business performance.

Efficiency Ratio and Adjusted Pre-Provision Net Revenue
The efficiency ratio measures operating expenses relative to revenue and provides insight into the cost of generating revenue. We adjust this ratio to exclude certain items that are not generally expected to recur frequently, as detailed in the accompanying schedule. These adjustments enhance comparability across reporting periods. Adjusted noninterest expense reflects how effectively we manage operating expenses, while adjusted pre-provision net revenue enables management and stakeholders to evaluate our capacity to generate capital. Additionally, taxable-equivalent net interest income facilitates comparability between revenue derived from taxable and tax-exempt sources.
